subject: Access handoff & JWT rotation patterns — PayZen integration
content:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>
To: Alex Martin <alex@payzen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Access handoff & JWT rotation patterns — PayZen integration

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great walkthrough of PayZen's reranking use case. This note covers the integration options we discussed for auth and key management, plus proposed next steps so your engineering team can unblock a short POC.

Summary of recommended approach (short):
- Primary: Service account + short-lived JWT (signed by your KMS) exchanged for Redwood access tokens. This gives you auditable, short-lived credentials and lets PayZen control key rotation.
- Fallback: Customer-managed API key scoped to a single model/route for quick dev testing (not recommended for production).

Why we favor service accounts + JWTs:
- No long-lived API keys to rotate manually; PayZen can rotate signing keys in KMS and issue new tokens immediately.
- Supports multi-region safe-rollout: tokens short TTL (e.g., 5m) means you can cut over signing keys without stale credentials.
- Works well with our SDKs (server SDKs exchange JWT -> session token transparently).

Key integration details we discussed:
- Token flow: Service account private key (in your KMS) signs a JWT -> Redwood token endpoint validates signature via your public key endpoint or JWKs -> returns short-lived access token for API calls.
- Rotation: publish new JWK set; Redwood caches JWKs for <60s TTL during rollout; we also support key id (kid) header to pick correct key.
- Canary routing: you can pin routes to old/new model variant while rotating keys; Redwood's routing policies allow per-route token acceptance for overlap windows.

Attachments: I attached a quick diagram and example service-account policy that Ben sketched out in the call.

Action items / next steps:
1) Engineering deep-dive (Ben + your infra): 60-min session to walk through JWT exchange and sample SDK integration. Proposed: Mon 9/13 10am PT.
2) Provide a temporary dev service account public JWK URL (or shared JWK file) so we can run a verification POC.
3) Agree TTL for tokens during POC (suggest 5m) and SLO for validation latency.

Let me know if the recommended approach matches expectations. Happy to pivot if your security team prefers OAuth client credentials flow instead — we support that too.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martin <alex@payzen.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access handoff & JWT rotation patterns — PayZen integration

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. The service-account + JWT approach looks sensible. A couple of clarifying Qs from our infra/security lead (Priya):

1) During key rotation, can Redwood accept tokens signed by both old and new keys for a limited overlap window? We want to avoid a hard fail when rotating keys.
2) How do you handle JWK caching — if we rotate keys frequently should we expect a propagation delay that causes auth failures?
3) For the POC, we'll host a JWK endpoint under our auth domain (https://auth.payzen.com/.well-known/jwks.json). Will you pull it, or do you prefer us to push the public JWK?

Also, can you share a minimal SDK snippet for the JWT exchange so our backend folks can review?

Appreciate it — Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>
To: Alex Martin <alex@payzen.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@payzen.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access handoff & JWT rotation patterns — PayZen integration

Alex / Priya — quick technical reply to the three points: good questions.

1) Overlap acceptance: yes. Redwood supports accepting tokens signed by multiple keys concurrently via the kid header. During rotation you can publish the new key and keep the old key available for a short window (configurable on your side). We recommend a 10–15 minute overlap for production rotations; for POC 1–2 minutes is usually fine.

2) JWK caching: our validation layer caches JWKs but polls for updates aggressively. Default behavior: cache for 60s, graceful backoff on failures. If you need near-zero delay we can configure webhook-based invalidation (we'll call an endpoint on your side when we detect a rotation) or you can set Cache-Control headers on the JWKs endpoint to advise shorter TTL. Expected propagation edge cases: if a signed token is issued before key revocation and still within token TTL, it remains valid until expiry.

3) JWK delivery: either hosting a JWKs endpoint (preferred) or uploading a public JWK to our console works. For the POC please host the endpoint — makes iterative testing easier.

Sample server-side flow (pseudo-snippet):
- backend creates JWT with sub=service-account-payzen, aud=redwood-token, exp=now+60s, kid=<key-id>
- sign JWT with KMS private key
- POST /v1/token/exchange {"grant_type":"urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer","assertion":<JWT>} -> returns access_token (TTL 5m)
- call /v1/generate with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

I'll attach the example service-account policy and a quick rotation diagram (see attachments).

Proposed time for deep-dive: Mon 9/13 10am PT works for me — added to the invite once you confirm.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
